signal_summary: The Sep 18 HYPE manual-borrow breakout was previously blocked from a confirmation add by negative weekly stablecoin flow, declining weekly spot volume and sharply elevated perp funding. Those blockers have now materially improved at the same time: Hyperliquid stablecoin supply is +4.37% over seven days, spot DEX volume is +11.03% weekly, perp volume is +26.46% weekly, TVL remains higher, and HYPE funding normalized from the prior 59.1% annualized snapshot to about 11.0% while price/usage persisted at a fresh all-time high. This clears the prior explicitly recorded confirmation trigger. A 2.5% NAV PAPER add is executed prospectively, bringing HYPE only to roughly 5.23% of NAV rather than the 7.5% cap because OI remains high, the October 6 unlock is large, and no fresh independent selective-wallet cohort was verified.

ecosystem_regime_evidence.rwa_interpretation: RWA AUM remains immaterial to this thesis; this signal is crypto trading, stablecoin capital stock, credit/collateral utility and protocol fee activity, not RWA issuance or RWA secondary-trading growth.
ecosystem_regime_evidence.relative_leadership: Hyperliquid is the cleanest marginal improvement among the major speculative ecosystems checked in this run. Robinhood Chain still has much larger spot turnover but its seven-day DEX volume is -12.50% and 24h inflow is negative; Solana seven-day DEX volume is -22.13%, stablecoin supply -4.44% and 24h inflow -$17.01M.

change_from_prior_hype_checkpoint.interpretation: The missing external-capital/spot-flow leg arrived and funding crowding improved sharply. OI did not normalize materially, so leverage risk remains a major caveat rather than a resolved issue.

derivatives_quality.interpretation: Funding fell from an extreme roughly 59.1% annualized prior snapshot to about 11.0% while price remained near record highs. This is materially healthier confirmation, but $2.01B OI still leaves meaningful two-sided liquidation reflexivity.

flow_quality_and_incentive_attribution.points_history: Hyperliquid's original points phase ended May 2024 and its L1 points phase ended November 2024.
flow_quality_and_incentive_attribution.routine_fee_incentives: Referral discounts and maker rebates remain part of the standing fee schedule and are therefore not treated as zero incentive contamination.
flow_quality_and_incentive_attribution.reason: The simultaneous stablecoin-stock increase, TVL growth, spot acceleration, perp acceleration and fee/revenue persistence is not primarily attributable to a new points, quest or airdrop campaign. Standing maker/referral economics are discounted but do not explain the abrupt change versus the prior checkpoint.

wallet_quality.note: No newly funded, historically selective independent HYPE spot-accumulator cohort was verified. Public whale headlines dominated by leveraged perp positions are not counted as selective spot accumulation.

value_capture.details: Hyperliquid's standing fee architecture directs fees to community destinations including the Assistance Fund, which automatically converts trading fees to HYPE and burns the HYPE. CoinGecko reports about $2.97M of 24h Hyperliquid fees and $2.42M of project revenue at this checkpoint. Manual borrowing itself is utility rather than direct HYPE-holder interest income; the fee-funded burn is the direct capture leg.

liquidity_executability.reason: HYPE has roughly $1.83B of 24h token turnover and broad venue depth. CoinGecko shows about $153K / $131K of +/-2% depth on the native HYPE/USDC venue alone, with substantially deeper CEX books. A roughly $268 paper add is trivial relative to executable liquidity; Tier A 0.15% simulated one-way cost applied.

caveats: Market cap is about $20.9B versus roughly $89.7B FDV, leaving large dilution overhang.
Next scheduled unlock is October 6: 9.92M HYPE, about $931M at the current mark and 1% of total supply, allocated to Core Contributors.
$2.01B of HYPE perp open interest remains high despite funding normalization.
HYPE-backed manual borrowing creates a collateral-liquidation feedback channel during downside moves.
The reported $269M borrowed on launch infrastructure is not cleanly decomposed between manual borrowing and existing portfolio-margin borrowing.
No fresh independent selective-wallet cohort was verified.

why_now: This is not an add simply because HYPE printed another all-time high. The Sep 18 no-add record named renewed stablecoin inflows plus persistent spot/fee growth and derivatives funding normalization as the specific confirmation needed. All three moved in the required direction before this trade: stablecoin growth flipped positive and strong, spot volume flipped from weekly contraction to expansion, perp activity accelerated, and funding fell from an extreme to a much more ordinary positive level. Because the wallet leg is still missing and the October 6 unlock is material, the position is increased by only one 2.5% confirmation tranche rather than to the 7.5% maximum.
major_uncertainties: The positive stablecoin and volume changes need persistence after the manual-borrow launch novelty window.
Open interest remains extremely large even though funding normalized.
No new selective-wallet cohort independently confirms the add.
The October 6 Core Contributor unlock is a large near-term supply event.
Current social attention is elevated near an all-time high, so influencer-driven momentum is discounted rather than counted as confirmation.
